questions.question: When and where did Thomas Hanrahan, born about 1840 in Ireland and living in Saratoga, New York, in 1880, marry Johanna Ryan (born about 1845 in Ireland)?
questions.rationale: The project has no questions yet and the objective is a single marriage event with two attributes (date and place), so it is the first question restated with identifying detail. The tree links the couple but records no marriage fact or source for it, and their children were born 1869-1872, which bounds the search window.

items.rationale: The tree holds Irish baptism entries naming Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan as parents of Mary (17 Feb 1871) and John (28 Nov 1872, Ardfinnan, County Tipperary), and the tree lists Mary's birth as Ireland. Their 1880 census residence in Saratoga is therefore not where the children were born; the couple were likely in Ireland by 1871, so a marriage there before 1871 is a prime candidate and Saratoga records alone would miss it. Plan a Catholic parish marriage search in Ardfinnan and neighboring Tipperary parishes, with spelling variants Hanrahan, Hanraghan, Hourigan, Ryan, Ryn and Johanna/Joanna/Hannah/Julia. No locality survey exists yet for Ireland: this item rests on the tree's baptism facts, and a locality survey of County Tipperary is recommended before it runs. Treat Ryan as the surname recorded for her in the baptisms, not yet confirmed as her birth name.

Companion to the parish search: Irish civil marriage registration index (e.g. the national civil records site, a free external site the researcher or search-external-sites would open) for a Thomas Hanrahan to Johanna Ryan marriage in the Tipperary registration districts around Ardfinnan. Would give an exact date, place and witnesses if registered. Same caveat: Ireland has no locality survey yet; locate the actual site through its own pages, not from memory.
items.skip_reason: IrishGenealogy.ie is not a supported site for URL building and needs a user capture, which no user present can make; FamilySearch holds the Irish civil registration indexes for search-records.

items.jurisdiction: New York City, New York, United States
items.rationale: The tree records Elizabeth (about 1869) and Thomas (about 1870) as born in New York, shown in the tree as New York City, while Mary and John have Irish births in 1871-1872: the family may have moved between New York and Ireland, or these tree birthplaces may be mistaken for another family (an open identity question). A marriage in New York City in the 1860s is therefore a candidate. The New York City marriage collection is name-searchable and New York, Marriages 1686-1980 and Church and Civil Marriages 1704-1995 are name-searchable statewide (loc_001); search with variant spellings.

loc_001 shows no civil marriage registration in Saratoga County for this period (county marriage records begin 1908), so Catholic parish registers under the Diocese of Albany are the main substitute. New York, Church and Civil Marriages, 1704-1995 and New York, Church Records, 1660-1954 are name-searchable but may not include the Catholic parish serving the couple; the parish itself is unconfirmed, so pair with an inquiry via the Diocese of Albany archives or the county wiki's Catholic church guide named in loc_001. Include neighboring counties named in loc_001 (Albany, Rensselaer, Washington, Warren, Montgomery, Fulton, Schenectady, Hamilton) as co-equal searches, not fallbacks.

The New York State Census 1865 is name-searchable for the household; its marriage schedule (end of each town's schedule in the images, per loc_001) covers only marriages in the year before June 1865, so a hit is a long shot but cheap and gives date, place and type of ceremony. Also check 1865 for the couple living together, which bounds the marriage date.

The 1880 census entry is in the tree (Thomas, Johannah, Elizabeth, Thomas, Mary, John all resident in Saratoga; Thomas born about 1840 in Ireland). Review the 1880 household image for years married or immigration clues if given, then search 1870 federal and the New York State Census 1875 (name-searchable) for the household, each child's stated birthplace and the parents' arrival years. This places the couple before or after emigration and decides whether to weight the Irish or New York marriage items.

FAN and derivative evidence: Thomas's naturalization papers (New York, County Naturalization Records, name-searchable; sized to the collection, as papers may be filed decades after marriage) state arrival date and sometimes the wife; the death, burial and obituary entries of Thomas and Johanna (New York State Death Index from 1880, cemetery abstracts, local newspapers) may name spouse, birthplace and a marriage anniversary; neighbors and Ryan relatives in the 1880 census and baptism sponsors in the Irish baptisms of Mary and John may point to the marriage parish.

items.rationale: Conflict-driven. The index entry for the 1 Feb 1868 Ballylooby Catholic marriage (ark:/61903/1:1:6267-W22Q) gives groom 'Thomam Hanrahan' and bride 'Johan Ryan' with no age, residence or parents. The matching civil entry (QGV8-PQK7, same date, Thomas Hanrahan and Judy Ryan) names the groom's father as John Hanrahan and the bride's father as Thomas Ryan. Ireland Catholic Parish Registers 1740-1900 is name-searchable, but the register image itself must be read for the fuller entry (residences, witnesses, any age or townland) that could tie the groom to, or exclude him from, the Saratoga Thomas Hanrahan (born about 1840 Ireland). Ballylooby is not Ardfinnan parish, so note the witnesses and townlands for FAN leads. Read the Latin entry and compare the spelling of the names to the index. Spelling variants Hanrahan, Hanraghan, Hourigan; Johanna, Judy, Joanna, Hannah.

Conflict-driven. The tree and indexed baptisms of Mary (17 Feb 1871, ark:/61903/1:1:F5GR-QBN) and John (28 Nov 1872, ark:/61903/1:1:F5YK-84C) name Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan as parents in Ardfinnan, while other tree facts put Elizabeth (about 1869) and Thomas (about 1870) in New York. Read the baptism register images for parents' full names, townland or residence, sponsors and any marginal notes, to judge whether they are the same couple as the Ballylooby 1868 marriage and our Saratoga family or a different Hanrahan household. Sponsors are FAN leads for the Ryan family and the marriage parish. Ardfinnan's register start date was not confirmed in loc_003, so check the register itself.

Conflict-driven. New York, Passenger Lists, 1820-1920 (collection 1849782) is name-searchable. A Thomas Hanrahan (with Johanna and young children) crossing between Ireland and New York would explain how a family appears in New York about 1869-1870 (the 1870 census lists Thomas Hanahan b. 1840 Ireland in Northumberland, Saratoga) yet has children baptised in Tipperary in 1871-72, and would give the arrival year and ship companions. Search with variants Hanrahan, Hanahan, Hanraghan, Hanrehan and Johanna/Joanna/Hannah. Note this covers arrivals at New York only; returns to Ireland leave no record here.

conflicts.independence_analysis: The 1870 and 1880 censuses both record the household through an unnamed household informant, so their age and birthplace entries repeat one unknown answer rather than two accounts. The Ballylooby marriage has a parish register entry (a_084) and a civil copy (a_095) of one event, counted as one unit. The new passenger list (src_007, a_149 to a_154) is a separate record created at arrival in New York in 1869, independent of the census and the Irish register. It names only a single man, Thos Hanahan, aged 28, born Ireland about 1841, and does not list a wife or children, so it bears on the head's identity and travel, not on the family's children.
conflicts.weighing_analysis: The 1880 census ages were the check to run first, and they do not support the proposed split. In 1880 Mary is recorded at 15, born about 1864-65 in New York (a_021, a_027). In 1870 the same household recorded Mary at 6, born about 1863-64 in New York (a_116, a_120). Those entries describe one girl ageing about nine years, so the census supports a single New York-born Mary across both censuses, not an Irish-born Mary of 1871. John is 8 in 1880, born about 1871-72 (a_048), which fits the 1872 Ardfinnan baptism by age but still carries a New York birthplace (a_052). Both censuses come from an unnamed household member, so their ages and birthplaces are indeterminate. The passenger list (src_007, a_149 to a_154) shows one Thos Hanahan, 28, from Ireland, arriving in 1869 with no family listed. If the New York-born children are genuine, a man arriving in 1869 must have had an earlier American stay the list does not show. The census never names Ryan, and the given names Thomas and Johanna are the only link between the Saratoga head and the Ballylooby groom. No record yet places the Saratoga household as the marriage couple, so the identity question stays open.
conflicts.resolution_rationale: The problem: whether the Ballylooby groom of 1 February 1868 is the Thomas Hanahan who headed the Northumberland, Saratoga household in 1870 and 1880. The answer decides whether the Mary, Elizabeth, Thomas and John in that household are this marriage's children. The Tipperary evidence is the parish marriage register, which names the groom as Thomam and the bride as Johan Ryan, and a civil copy of the same entry, which names the bride's father as Thomas Ryan and the bride as Judy Ryan. Both are primary records of one event. The Saratoga evidence is the 1870 and 1880 censuses, which give the head's birthplace as Ireland and the children's as New York, and the 1869 arrival of a Thos Hanahan from Ireland. The census entries came from an unnamed household member, and the arrival list names one man with no family. Neither side can be set aside under the defensible rationales: the Irish marriage is not an uncorroborated single item, and the census is not an error-prone secondary source for the identity question. The 1880 ages show the same Mary across two censuses, so the simple explanation of a deceased older sibling is not supported. The likeliest explanations remain a census birthplace error by an informant who did not know the Irish or New York history of the family, a second Thomas Hanrahan in New York, or an earlier union. Decisive records: the Ballylooby 1868 register image (groom's age, residence, father's name, witnesses), which is blocked in this run; New York arrival records for a Johanna Ryan or a Hanahan family showing a wife and children travelling 1869-1872; the 1875 New York State census page for Northumberland, Saratoga, to see whether Mary and John are in the household; and Catholic baptisms in Saratoga or Northumberland for 1862-1866 naming a Mary and a James to a Thomas and Johanna. New York's 1847-1849 local registration law was poorly enforced and lapsed after a few years, and statewide registration only began 1880-1881 with compliance incomplete until 1913; for marriages the FamilySearch Wiki gives general compliance only by 1880, meaning even 1880s civil marriage records for this county may be thin (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Vital_Records).

Saratoga County parishes fall under the Diocese of Albany; the FamilySearch Wiki names no specific parish serving the Hanrahan/Ryan couple, so the actual Catholic parish of marriage is unconfirmed — consult the Diocese of Albany archives or the Local Catholic Church guide cited on the county wiki page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy#Church_Records).

New York State 1865 and 1875 state censuses include a Marriage schedule covering marriages in the 12 months before the census (ending 1 June of the census year) with husband/wife names, ages, prior marital status, and date/place of marriage and type of ceremony — browse to the end of each town's population schedule in the FamilySearch images for these years (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy#Census_Records).

Some couples eloped to other New York 'Gretna Green' locations (e.g. Niagara Falls, Buffalo, Ogdensburgh) or out of state rather than marry at home — if no local marriage record is found, consider these alternate venues (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Vital_Records#Marriage_Records).

No known history of courthouse disasters/record loss is reported for Saratoga County itself, but no civil marriage records exist for this period regardless, per the registration-date quirk above.

# Locality Guide: Saratoga County, New York (1860-1890)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** February 7, 1791, from Albany County (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy)
- **County seat:** Ballston Spa
- **Parent jurisdiction:** New York
- **Population during period:** 1860: 51,729; 1870: 51,529 (-0.4%); 1880: 55,156 (+7.0%); 1890: 57,663 (+4.5%) (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy)
- **Economy:** Mineral-spring resort tourism (Saratoga Springs) and mixed agriculture/small manufacturing, with the Champlain and Erie Canals (opened 1823/1825) and the Hudson/Mohawk river corridor channeling settlement and migration through the county.
- **Ethnic composition:** The FamilySearch Wiki's Irish-specific collection "U.S. Famine Irish Passenger Index, 1846-1851" is curated for New York State broadly, consistent with substantial Irish Catholic immigration into the Albany/Saratoga corridor during this period; no county-specific ethnic breakdown was returned by these tools.
- **Religious denominations:** Baptist, Episcopal, Methodist Episcopal, Reformed Protestant Dutch, and Society of Friends (Quaker) congregations are documented from the 1700s-1800s; Catholic parishes in the county fall under the Diocese of Albany (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy#Church_Records).
- **Key historical events:** No courthouse disasters or county-specific record losses are reported for Saratoga County (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy#Record_Loss).

## Boundary changes
- Saratoga County was created from Albany County on 7 February 1791 and has not since been divided; no boundary changes affecting it are reported for 1860-1890 (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy#Boundary_Changes).
- Earlier (pre-1791) records of this area are filed under Albany County.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** City/town/village level 1847 (poorly enforced, lapsed after a few years); state level 1880-1881; general compliance for marriages by 1880, but Saratoga County's own record-dates chart gives county marriage records beginning only in 1908 (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Vital_Records; https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy).
- **What exists:** For 1860-1890 there is effectively no civil marriage record series for Saratoga County — the 1847 law lapsed and county-level marriage records do not begin until 1908. "New York, County Marriages, 1778-1848; 1908-1937" (collection 1618491, index & images, 6,491,569 persons) covers only outside this window.
- **Where held:** Town/village clerks held any surviving 1847-era marriage records locally; none are known to survive in indexed form for Saratoga County in this window.
- **Gaps:** No county or state civil marriage record covers 1860-1890 for this county — this is the central obstacle to the research question.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church marriage records (see below) and the 1865/1875 state census marriage schedules are the primary substitutes for this period.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Baptist, Episcopal, Methodist Episcopal, Reformed Protestant Dutch, Society of Friends (1700s-1800s); Catholic parishes under the Diocese of Albany (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy#Church_Records).
- **Record types:** Marriages, baptisms, burials; "New York, Church and Civil Marriages, 1704-1995" (collection 2373836, 41,948 persons) and "New York, Church Records, 1660-1954" (collection 2787817, 303,598 persons) are statewide FamilySearch index collections that may include Saratoga County entries.
- **Where held:** Non-Catholic denominations have published/online abstracts via NYGenWeb (e.g., Old Reformed Dutch Church of Schuylerville marriages 1790-1857; Schuylerville Methodist Episcopal marriages 1854-1869) at http://saratoganygenweb.com/churchrc.htm. Catholic parish registers are held by the individual parishes under the Diocese of Albany; no FamilySearch Wiki result names which specific parish served Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan — this is unconfirmed and must be determined separately.
- **Gaps:** No digitized Catholic parish marriage register for Saratoga County surfaced in this survey; volume_search found county Presbyterian marriage volumes (Ballston Center 1783-1865; Charlton 1801-1862) but none specifically Catholic.
- **Language:** English for the denominations surveyed.

### Census records
- **Federal/national census:** 1860, 1870, 1880, 1890 (1890 largely destroyed nationwide by fire, a nationwide loss not specific to this county) (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy#Census_Records).
- **State/provincial census:** New York State censuses of 1855, 1865, 1875, 1892 — the 1865 and 1875 censuses include Marriage schedules covering marriages in the 12 months before the census (husband/wife names, ages, prior marital status, date/place of marriage, type of ceremony), browsable via FamilySearch Images after the population schedule for each town (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy#Census_Records).
- **Other enumerations:** New York Census of Inmates in Almshouses and Poorhouses, 1830-1920 (Ancestry).
- **Access:** 1855/1865/1875/1892 state censuses are indexed & images at FamilySearch; marriage/mortality schedules within the 1865 and 1875 censuses are browse-only images, not separately indexed.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, administrations, guardianships, probate petitions.
- **Testate or intestate:** Unknown for Thomas Hanrahan/Johanna Ryan; both series should be checked if either died in Saratoga County.
- **Date range:** From 1791 (county formation); FamilySearch Library microfilm includes a General index 1878-1904, Letters of administration 1815-1929, Wills 1791-1921 (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy#Probate_Records).
- **Where held:** Saratoga County Surrogate Court, Ballston Spa.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Not detailed by these tools for Saratoga County specifically.
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Not stated by the wiki pages fetched; see New York Land and Property for general guidance.
- **Types:** Deeds, land records; "New York, Land Records, 1630-1975" (collection 2078654, index & images, 135,738,899 persons).
- **Date range:** 1791 (county formation) per the record-dates chart.
- **Where held:** Saratoga County Clerk's office (also holds marriage, divorce, and court records) (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy#County_Courthouse).

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Civil War (1861-1865) falls within this period.
- **Record types:** Town clerks' registers of Civil War servicemen (available for Ballston, Charlton, Clifton Park, Corinth, Edinburg, Galway, Greenfield, Halfmoon, Providence, Saratoga Springs, Stillwater, Waterford, Wilton); service records, muster rolls.
- **Where held:** Originals at New York State Archives, Albany; microfilm at FamilySearch Library (FS Library Film 1993401-37); indexed at Ancestry (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy#Military_Records).

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Not individually named by these tools beyond the Gerald B.H. Solomon Saratoga National Cemetery.
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave, BillionGraves, Interment.net, Names in Stone, NYGenWeb Cemeteries, Tombstone Transcription Project — all listed for Saratoga County on the FamilySearch Wiki.
- **Physical records:** "New York, Cemetery Abstracts, 1800-1965" (collection 2552111, index & images, 251,828 persons).

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Saratoga Sentinel (index to marriage/death notices 1819-1837); The Saratogian (index 1999-present, includes marriages, at Saratoga Springs Public Library).
- **Where held:** "10,000 Vital Records of Eastern New York, 1777-1834" and "New York Marriage Notices, 1800-1855" and "New York Marriage Newspaper Extracts (Barber Collection), 1801-1880" at Ancestry ($); none of these newspaper abstract series extend into 1860-1890 for marriages specifically.
- **Content value:** Marriage notices can substitute for missing civil records but none of the indexed newspaper marriage series found cover the 1860-1890 window for this county.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Not a port county itself, but as Irish immigrants, Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan likely arrived via New York City; "US Famine Irish Passenger Index, 1846-1851" (FamilySearch, also at Ancestry/MyHeritage) and "New York Passenger Lists, 1820-1920" / "New York, Passenger Arrival Lists (Ellis Island), 1892-1925" are relevant statewide series.
- **Record types:** Passenger lists, naturalization petitions.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch, Ancestry, MyHeritage (indexed & images for most listed series).
- **Content note:** Examine full manifests for all family members traveling together, including children.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Assessment rolls (e.g., koha:164757, Saratoga County Assessor's 1840 assessment roll, FamilySearch Library).
- **Date range:** Earliest located in this survey is 1840; no 1860-1890 tax roll specifically surfaced.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch Library (microfilm/catalog); Saratoga County Clerk/Historian offices for originals.
- **Substitute value:** Can help place the family geographically between censuses, standing in for a missing 1890 census.

### Other record types
- Naturalization: "New York, County Naturalization Records, 1791-1980" (index & images) and "New York, Record of Naturalized Voters Registered, 1872-1878" (index & images) — relevant if Thomas Hanrahan naturalized in Saratoga County.

## Research tips
- No civil marriage record exists for Saratoga County covering 1860-1890 — county marriage records begin only in 1908 per the FamilySearch Wiki's own Saratoga County record-dates chart (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy#Saratoga_County,_New_York_Record_Dates) — so civil records cannot answer this question; pursue church and census substitutes first.
- Check the 1865 and 1875 New York State Census marriage schedules (browse to the end of each town's population schedule) for a marriage recorded in the 12 months before the census (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy#Census_Records).
- Couples sometimes married away from home at a "Gretna Green" location such as Niagara Falls, Buffalo, or Ogdensburgh, New York, rather than locally (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Vital_Records#Marriage_Records).
- Determine the specific Catholic parish serving the family before searching church registers — this survey found none named for Saratoga County; the Diocese of Albany holds parish jurisdiction, and the "Local Catholic Church and Family History" research guide cited on the county wiki page is the next step to identify the parish (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy#Church_Records).
- Search neighboring counties (Albany, Fulton, Hamilton, Montgomery, Rensselaer, Schenectady, Warren, Washington) as well, since an Irish immigrant couple could have married just across the county line.
- Use the 1860, 1870, and 1880 federal censuses to track the couple's residence and establish a town/parish to search for church marriage records, noting 1890 census loss is nationwide, not county-specific.

# Locality Guide: New York City, New York (Manhattan / New York County), 1855-1875 (1855-1875)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** New York (Manhattan) County was created in 1683 from the earlier "Yorkshire" jurisdiction; Orange County was briefly attached (1693-1698). It gained West Bronx in 1874, and the five boroughs were consolidated into New York City only in 1898 — after the target period. ([Manhattan Borough, New York Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Manhattan_Borough,_New_York_Genealogy))
- **County seat / administrative center:** New York City (Manhattan); courthouse at 60 Centre St.
- **Parent jurisdiction:** New York State, United States
- **Population during period:** 813,669 in 1860; 942,292 in 1870 — rapid immigrant-driven growth ([Manhattan Borough, New York Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Manhattan_Borough,_New_York_Genealogy))
- **Economy:** Dominant port and commercial city; heavy Irish and German immigrant labor force in this period.
- **Ethnic composition:** Large Irish Catholic and German immigrant populations settled from the 1840s famine years onward; this directly shapes which churches a couple like Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan (Irish-born) would have used for a marriage record.
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic (Archdiocese of New York), Dutch Reformed, Lutheran, Episcopal/Trinity Parish, and others were all active in Manhattan in this period.
- **Key historical events:** none specifically affecting record creation found in this survey beyond ordinary administrative growth.

## Boundary changes
- No boundary change affects the target period's marriage records: New York County's borders were stable from 1698 until 1874 (West Bronx added) and the five-borough consolidation (1898) postdates the window.
- Record Loss: the FamilySearch Wiki states there is no known history of courthouse disasters for this county ([Manhattan Borough, New York Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Manhattan_Borough,_New_York_Genealogy)).

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil marriage)
- **Start date:** New York City began its own municipal marriage registration in 1829, far earlier than the rest of the state (where statewide civil marriage registration began only in 1880, with compliance incomplete until 1913) — level: municipality, 1829 ([New York Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Vital_Records)). The NYC Metropolitan Board of Health (created 1866) formalized marriage-certificate collection.
- **What exists:** FamilySearch's "New York, New York City Marriage Records, 1829-1938" (collection 2143225, 16,963,079 people) is index-only at FamilySearch; the New York City Municipal Archives' "Historical Vital Records of NYC" site (https://a860-historicalvitalrecords.nyc.gov/) covers 1855-1949 with index & images and is the recommended first stop for an 1855-1875 marriage.
- **Where held:** Originals are at the NYC Municipal Archives / City Clerk (marriages), 31 Chambers St / 141 Worth St, New York, NY — New York State does NOT hold New York City vital records ([New York Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Vital_Records)).
- **Gaps:** FamilySearch's own digitized marriage-certificate volumes for Manhattan from this period (e.g. 1869, 1871-1873 certificate books, imageGroupNumbers 007587108/007589970/007590459/007590467) show 0 cataloged images online and no name index — browse/order only.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** none needed (NYC civil marriage registration already covers 1855-1875), but church records remain essential as NYC civil marriage records before 1880 are not always complete.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Roman Catholic (Archdiocese of New York), Dutch Reformed, Lutheran, Episcopal (Trinity Parish), Methodist — Manhattan parishes fall under the Archdiocese of New York ([Manhattan Borough, New York Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Manhattan_Borough,_New_York_Genealogy)).
- **Record types:** baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations.
- **Where held:** Most Catholic parish registers have not been centralized; the researcher must identify the specific parish and write to it, or to the Archdiocese of New York archives if the parish has closed. The Archdiocese has partnered with Findmypast to digitize and index pre-1918 baptismal and marriage registers (the "Catholic Heritage Archive") ([New York Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Church_Records)). FamilySearch's catalog search for marriage records tied to New York County returned only one hit in this survey — a Dutch Reformed Church, Greenwich Village marriages index (1808-1859, catalog id koha:281377) — a cataloguing gap, not evidence Catholic registers don't exist.
- **Gaps:** No tool result in this survey names the specific parish Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan attended — this is unconfirmed and must be established separately (city directories, baptism records of their children, etc.) before ordering parish records.
- **Language:** Catholic registers of this period are often in Latin; some German/Dutch congregation registers are in those languages.

### Census records
- **Federal census:** 1860 and 1870 US censuses cover the period (no marriage information, but useful to locate the family and corroborate an approximate marriage date via children's ages/birthplaces).
- **State census:** New York State Censuses exist for 1855, 1865, and 1875 (FamilySearch collections 1937366, 1491284, 1918735) and the 1865/1875 versions carry a marriage schedule for marriages in the prior 12 months — but coverage of New York City in these state census collections needs to be checked ward by ward; one external index found in this survey specifically covers "New York State Census, New York City Ward 17, 1855" at Findmypast, suggesting NYC coverage is ward-specific rather than uniform.
- **Other enumerations:** 1890 NYC Police Census (collection 2381996) postdates the period.
- **Access:** 1855/1865/1875 state censuses are indexed & images at FamilySearch and Ancestry.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** wills, administrations — not directly relevant to proving a marriage, but can confirm a wife's name/relationship.
- **Where held:** New York County Surrogate's Court; no specific holdings for this couple were identified in this survey.

### Land records
- Not surveyed as central to the marriage question; New York Land Records, 1630-1975 (collection 2078654) exists for the county if needed later.

### Military records
- Not applicable to the marriage question for this period beyond general note that Civil War service/pension files (1861-1865) sometimes give marriage dates/places; "New York, Civil War Service Records of Union Soldiers, 1861-1865" (collection 1932388) exists if Thomas Hanrahan served.

### Cemetery records
- FindAGrave and "New York, Cemetery Abstracts, 1800-1965" (collection 2552111) are available but not matched to this couple in this survey.

### Newspaper records
- The "NYC Marriage & Death Notices 1857-1868" collection at the New York Society Library, and Ancestry's "Index to Marriages and Deaths in the New York Herald" (vols. covering 1835-1863), are candidate sources for a marriage notice if the family had any social prominence; otherwise unlikely for an Irish immigrant laboring family.

### Immigration/emigration records
- As Irish immigrants, Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan likely arrived via the Port of New York; the "US Famine Irish Passenger Index, 1846-1851" (FamilySearch collection 2110821) or general NY passenger list collections (1820-1891, collection 1849782) could place their arrival, though this is before the marriage question itself.

### Tax records
- Not surveyed in depth; county tax records could substitute for census years but were not matched to this family in this survey.

### Other record types
- City directories (NYC directories 1786-1922 at Fold3) can help locate the couple's residence/occupation and narrow which parish or ward to search.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | New York, New York City Marriage Records, 1829-1938 (index only); New York, Church and Civil Marriages, 1704-1995 (index incomplete); New York, Marriages, 1686-1980 (index only); New York, County Marriages, 1778-1848/1908-1937 | Core NYC civil marriage index for 1855-1875 | Free |
| NYC Municipal Archives (Historical Vital Records of NYC) | NYC marriages 1855-1949 with index & images | Image access to original NYC marriage certificates | Free (https://a860-historicalvitalrecords.nyc.gov/) |
| Findmypast | New York Roman Catholic Parish Marriages (index & images); Catholic Heritage Archive (pre-1918 Archdiocese of New York baptism/marriage registers) | Catholic parish marriage registers, the most likely record type for this Irish Catholic couple | Subscription (https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/new-york-roman-catholic-parish-marriages) |
| Ancestry | New York, New York, Extracted Marriage Index, 1866-1937; New York City, Compiled Marriage Index, 1600s-1800s | Name-indexed marriage index covering part of the period | Subscription |
| German Genealogy Group | New York City Grooms Index / Brides Index, 1864-1937 | Free index covering the tail end of the period (1864-1875) | Free (http://www.germangenealogygroup.com/records-search/grooms.php) |

**Coverage of this survey:** A FamilySearch volume_search for New York County marriage/religious-marriage material, 1855-1875, returned 39 digitized volumes as a complete result set (not a partial page); 8 are browse-only, 25 are full-text searchable but not name-indexed, and several (1869, 1871-1873 Manhattan marriage certificate books) show zero cataloged images online.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| NYC Municipal Archives | Original NYC birth, marriage, and death records, 1855-1949 | 31 Chambers Street, New York; online ordering at https://dorisorders.nyc.gov/ |
| NYC Office of the City Clerk | Marriage records (originals) | 141 Worth Street, New York; mail-in request form |
| Archdiocese of New York Archives | Catholic parish sacramental registers for closed/merged parishes | Parish Finder at https://archny.org/parish-finder/; contact individual parishes directly for active ones |
| New York State Archives | Indexes only to NY vital records (not NYC originals) | Albany, NY — write/email archinfo@nysed.gov |

## Records NOT online
- Original NYC marriage certificates for several years within 1855-1875 (including certificate books for 1869, 1871, 1872, 1873 identified in this survey) have zero digitized/indexed images on FamilySearch — they exist only as physical or microfilm holdings to browse or order from the NYC Municipal Archives.
- Most individual Catholic parish marriage registers have not been centralized online outside the Findmypast Catholic Heritage Archive/Roman Catholic Parish Marriages index; many parishes' records remain with the parish or Archdiocese archive only.

## Known record losses
- The FamilySearch Wiki states there is no known history of courthouse disasters for New York (Manhattan) County ([Manhattan Borough, New York Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Manhattan_Borough,_New_York_Genealogy)); no record loss specific to this county's marriage records was found in this survey.

## Research tips
- New York City's own marriage registration began in 1829, well before statewide civil registration (1880) — so unlike many NY counties, a civil marriage record is plausible for 1855-1875 and should be checked first via the NYC Municipal Archives' "Historical Vital Records of NYC" site, which has index & images for 1855-1949 ([New York Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Vital_Records)).
- Because the family is Irish Catholic, check the Findmypast Catholic Heritage Archive and "New York Roman Catholic Parish Marriages" index once a specific parish or neighborhood of residence is identified ([New York Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Church_Records)).
- If no marriage record turns up in NYC, consider that the couple may have married in Ireland before emigrating, in another New York county en route, or eloped to a recognized New York "Gretna Green" such as Niagara Falls, Ogdensburgh, or Buffalo ([New York Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Vital_Records)).
- Many of FamilySearch's digitized NYC marriage volumes for this period are full-text searchable but not name-indexed — use FamilySearch's full-text search tool rather than relying only on the standard person-search index.
- City directories can help pin down an approximate address/ward for the couple around 1869-1870 (when their New York-born children appear), narrowing which parish or ward's marriage records to search.
- The New York State censuses of 1865 and 1875 carry marriage schedules for marriages in the prior year — worth checking if the marriage occurred close to those census dates, though NYC's ward-level coverage in these collections should be verified first.

# Locality Guide: Ardfinnan, County Tipperary, Ireland (1855-1875)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** County Tipperary dates from the early 13th century (Norman invasion era); it was long divided administratively into North Tipperary (seat Nenagh) and South Tipperary (seat Clonmel), reunited as one local authority in 2012. Ardfinnan lies in South Tipperary. (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/County_Tipperary,_Ireland_Genealogy)
- **County town / administrative centers:** Nenagh (north), Clonmel (south)
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Ireland (Munster province)
- **Population during period:** 331,567 in 1851 (post-Famine decline from 435,553); continued falling for decades (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/County_Tipperary,_Ireland_Genealogy)
- **Religious composition:** in 1871, 93.8% Roman Catholic, 5.4% Church of Ireland, 0.3% each Presbyterian and Methodist (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/County_Tipperary,_Ireland_Genealogy)
- **Key historical context:** the county was devastated by the Great Famine (1845-1852), driving the population decline and heavy emigration that continued through the 1855-1875 period researched here.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Marriage registration began nationally in 1845 for non-Catholic marriages only; registration was extended to ALL marriages (Catholic included) in 1864. Birth and death registration also began nationally in 1864. (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Civil_Registration)
- **What exists:** Civil marriage registers record marriage date and place, names/ages/occupations/marital status of bride and groom, residences, fathers' names and occupations, denomination of the church, and signatures of bride, groom and witnesses (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Civil_Registration)
- **Where held:** "Ireland, Civil Registration, 1845-1913" (index & images, FamilySearch collection 2659409) and "Ireland, Civil Registration Indexes, 1845-1958" (index only, collection 1408347); also IrishGenealogy.ie (index & images, marriages 1845-1948)
- **Gaps:** For a Catholic marriage before 1864, there is NO civil record at all — only the parish register. Civil registration is organized by registration district, not townland, so the index alone will not pin the precise townland; the original entry must be checked.
- **Pre-registration/parallel alternatives:** Catholic parish (church) marriage registers are the primary and, before 1864, the only source.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Overwhelmingly Roman Catholic (93.8% in 1871), with a Church of Ireland minority (5.4%) and small Presbyterian/Methodist communities (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/County_Tipperary,_Ireland_Genealogy)
- **Record types:** Baptism, marriage, and burial registers; Catholic registers rarely include burials
- **Where held:** "Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1740-1900" at FamilySearch (collection 2820100, index & images, 27+ million people) and at Ancestry (collection 61039); the National Library of Ireland holds the originals/microfilm of Catholic parish registers (https://registers.nli.ie/). volume_search located specific Tipperary parish marriage/baptism volumes (e.g. Bournea and Corbally, Moneygall/Cullenwaine, Borrisokane, Cloughjordan) spanning the 1855-1875 period, but Ardfinnan's own volume was not individually returned in this survey.
- **Ardfinnan parish specifically:** A FamilySearch Wiki guide page exists for "Ardfinnan Catholic Parish, County Tipperary" pointing researchers to the free johngrenham.com Irish Ancestors site for that parish's specific record coverage and a search-strategy outline (start with the child's birth, find siblings, then work back to the parents' marriage) (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ardfinnan_Catholic_Parish,_County_Tipperary,_Ireland_Genealogy)
- **Gaps:** Most rural Catholic parish registers across Ireland begin only around Catholic Emancipation (1828) or later; no tool result in this survey confirmed Ardfinnan's own register start year — this must be checked directly in the register or catalog entry.
- **Language:** Catholic registers are frequently in Latin; FamilySearch provides a Latin Word List for translation (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Latin_Word_List)

### Census records
- **Federal/national census:** No Irish census returns survive in full for 1855-1875 — only the 1901 and 1911 censuses survive whole nationally (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Getting_Started). Earlier census fragments exist for some areas but none were returned for Tipperary/Ardfinnan in this survey.
- **Other enumerations:** Griffith's Valuation (1847-1864) and the Valuation Office Books (1831-1856, FamilySearch collection 2329951, index & images) substitute as property/household listings for this period.
- **Access:** 1901/1911 census: indexed with images at FamilySearch (collections 1626180, 2854327). Valuation records: indexed with images.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, administrations, marriage license bonds/bonds indexes
- **Date range:** "Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623-1866" (collection 3460239) and "Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Wills & Administrations Indexes, 1595-1858" (collection 3460908) both cover part of this period
- **Where held:** FamilySearch (index & images for the marriage bonds); originals historically held by diocesan/prerogative courts, with most pre-1922 original wills destroyed in the Public Record Office fire — the Betham, Crossle, and Thrift genealogical abstracts are cited substitutes (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Townland-based valuation surveys rather than metes-and-bounds deeds for ordinary families
- **Types:** Griffith's Valuation (1847-1864), Valuation Office Books (1831-1856), Tithe Applotment Books (1824-1855, collection 1804886)
- **Where held:** FamilySearch (indexed & images for Valuation Office Books); Ancestry and MyHeritage also host Griffith's Valuation; National Archives of Ireland hosts the Tithe Applotment Books online free

### Military records
- No specific Tipperary militia/service record collections for 1855-1875 were returned by this survey beyond the general "Scotland, Ireland and Wales Militia Attestation Papers, 1800-1915" at Ancestry; the county's Royal Irish Constabulary occupational records (1816-1921) may also be relevant if the family's men served.

### Cemetery records
- No Tipperary-specific cemetery collection date ranges covering 1855-1875 were returned; "Ireland Cemetery Collection, 1865-2023" at Ancestry (index only) and general Find a Grave coverage are the nearest available.

### Newspaper records
- No Tipperary-specific newspaper title/date range was returned by this survey; national Irish newspaper marriage-notice indexes exist at Findmypast ($) as a possible substitute for a formal marriage record.

### Immigration/emigration records
- Given the couple's eventual residence in Saratoga, New York (per the project's objective), passenger list and emigration record searches (e.g. "Irish Passenger Lists, 1847-1871" at Ancestry) are relevant — examine full manifests, which list every family member including children.

### Tax records
- Tithe Applotment Books (1824-1855) and Valuation Office Books (1831-1856) substitute for missing census years and can establish family residence in a specific townland before and into this period.

### Other record types
- National School Registers, 1847-1954 (collection 4496116) may show children of the family if they remained in Ireland past 1855; Petty Sessions Court Registers, 1828-1912 (collection 2487287) are a large county-level court record series that can place individuals locally.

## Research tips
- Civil registration of Catholic marriages did not begin until 1864, so a Hanrahan-Ryan marriage anywhere from 1855 to 1863 will only be found in a Catholic parish register, never in civil records (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Civil_Registration).
- Even after 1864, the civil registration index organizes entries by registration district, not townland or parish — a promising index hit should always be checked against the original register image to confirm the actual place (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Civil_Registration#Registration_Districts).
- Marriages were usually recorded in the bride's home parish, so if Johanna Ryan's family resided in a different parish than Ardfinnan, search there first for the marriage entry (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Civil_Registration).
- Follow the standard Irish research sequence recommended for this parish: start from the two known Ardfinnan baptisms (1871, 1872), then search for siblings' baptisms in the same register, then work back to find the parents' marriage entry, which typically appears shortly before the earliest known child (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ardfinnan_Catholic_Parish,_County_Tipperary,_Ireland_Genealogy).
- If Ardfinnan's own Catholic register does not show the marriage, search the neighboring Catholic parishes as well — Catholic parish boundaries did not match civil parish boundaries, so "neighboring" must be read from a Catholic parish map, not the civil parish map (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records).
- Catholic registers are commonly in Latin; use the FamilySearch Latin Word List when reading entries (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Latin_Word_List).
- This survey did not confirm Ardfinnan's own register start date or its specific online image/index coverage — check the johngrenham.com Irish Ancestors page for Ardfinnan directly, and confirm via FamilySearch's "Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1740-1900" collection search.
